messages:
emma: ran a short bring-up for aurora9b int8 vs fp16 focused on multi-paragraph summarization and citation fidelity. posting compact numbers + two pragmatic rollout patterns. :memo:
kai: drop the numbers pls
emma: quick snapshot (slice=multi-par-article, avg input ~980 tokens, N=480):
```
- p95 latency: fp16 200ms | int8 245ms
- tokens/sec: fp16 0.95 | int8 0.41
- cost per 1k tokens: fp16 $0.0085 | int8 $0.0036
- recall@5 (golded): fp16 79.0% | int8 73.6%  (delta -5.4pp)
- ROUGE-L drop: ~4.0 pts
- hallucination heuristic spike: fp16 1.9% | int8 6.3%
```
link: https://internal.redwood/sparkbench/aurora9b/3177770000
marta: econ takeaway: ~2.36x unit token savings. for a 2M token-month job that's roughly $6.9k -> $16.0k saving. big on cost but quality risk for onboarding/legal flows.
ryan: product note: multi-par article summaries are ~10% of calls but represent ~45% of retention-sensitive flows. can't ignore a ~5pp recall drop.
kai: pragmatic mitigations: 1) length+priming hybrid routing 2) KV prefix caching for long contexts 3) micro-canary w/ parallel fp16 probes to measure live delta. pseudo-rule below.
```
# hybrid routing example
if request.tokens > 700 or priming_docs >= 2:
  route -> fp16
elif novelty_score < 0.55:
  route -> fp16
else:
  route -> int8
```
emma: rollout plan suggestion: a) 5% global canary where int8 default, but we mirror long-par requests to fp16 (no impact) for 72h b) a 3% live probe that routes long-par 20%->fp16 to test user-facing quality c) auto-fallback policy if recall_delta > 3.0pts for 6h
ryan: i'll prepare an econ slide: cost delta, projected retention sensitivity scenarios (0.5% retention per 1pt recall loss baseline), and fallback cost assumptions.
marta: ops note: enable KV cache + run chunked decode microbench in parallel. if caching reduces fp16 spend by 30%, the econ shifts.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary created: aurora9b-int8-mirror @5% with parallel fp16 probe; probe job id 3177770000. See https://internal.redwood/deploys/3177770000
emma: thanks all. i'll post the 24h snapshot here and add a few sample failure cases separately. :mag:
